mainTopic: Combining the reading and spelling of a פסוק, and the source for בית הלל that one placement of blood is enough for a חטאת, defended through the three times וְכִפֶּר
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how the mentions of סכת teach three walls for a סוכה, with a הלכה למשה מסיני reducing the third wall to a טפח. It then asks why we don't combine the reading and the spelling of שבעים, which would make a mother of a girl טמאה for forty-two days. The answer is that the word כנדתה shows the פסוק counts in weeks. Next, a ברייתא gives a source for בית הלל that one placement of blood works even for a חטאת. Logic could compare the animal חטאת to the bird חטאת or to the inner חטאות, and the two comparisons tie. So the three times וְכִפֶּר, which are extra because וְנִסְלַח already teaches atonement, teach that three, two, or even one placement is enough. The גמרא tests other readings of those words, such as blood put below or split above and below. רבא answers that the three words match the corners, and the גמרא adds that blood is never split half above and half below. It defends that rule against the יום כיפור sprinklings, which were done like whip strokes. The amud ends with a new challenge from the seven sprinklings on טׇהֳרוֹ of the מזבח, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How the סוכה verses add up to three walls, with the third only a טפח
steps.stepSummary: One mention of סוכה teaches the basic מצוה and one teaches that it needs סכך. That leaves three walls, and a הלכה למשה מסיני reduces the third wall to a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, one mention is entirely for the מצוה itself, and one is for the covering. The הלכה came and reduced the third wall, and set it at a handbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question about how many walls a סוכה needs. It explains how the mentions of the word סכת are counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every mention of סכת counts toward walls. One is used up teaching the מצוה of living in a סוכה, and one teaches that it needs a covering (סכך). The rest point to three walls, and an oral tradition from סיני says the third wall only has to be a טפח.

the covering of the סוכה
a הלכה למשה מסיני, an oral law from סיני
reduced it
a handbreadth

phrases.english: There, one mention in the verse

steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-counting the mentions: some are used for other teachings, and a הלכה למשה מסיני adjusts the last wall.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each mention of סכת might count as a separate wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two mentions are used for other laws. The three left teach three walls, and the third one only needs to be a טפח.

steps.title: If both reading and spelling count, a mother of a girl should be impure forty-two days
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק שבעים can be read as two weeks (14 days) or, from its spelling, as seventy days. If both count, she should be טמאה for the middle number, 42 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so: 'then she shall be impure two weeks' can be read as 'seventy.' Let the reading have its effect and the spelling have its effect, and she should need to sit forty-two days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea of combining the reading and the spelling. It points to a case where doing that gives a result nobody holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שבעים is read as 'two weeks' (14 days), but its letters could also spell 'seventy.' If we always combine the two, we would land in the middle at 42 days. No one says a woman is טמאה for 42 days, so the method seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so (introduces a challenge)
two weeks
seventy
the spelling, the written letters
to sit, meaning to stay in טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: In step 1, קרא meant 'a mention in the verse.' Here קרא means the way the word is read aloud (the מקרא), in contrast to מסורת, the way it is spelled.

phrases.english: But if so,
'then she shall be impure two weeks'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:5, about a woman who gives birth to a girl.

phrases.english: can be read as 'seventy';
let the reading have its effect and let the spelling have its effect,
so she should need to sit forty-two days!
phrases.notes: 42 is exactly halfway between 14 and 70.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the method used in step 1 against a different פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The method of combining the reading and the spelling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applying the method to שבעים gives 42 days of טומאה, which no one holds.

steps.title: The word 'as in her menstruation' shows the verse means weeks
steps.stepSummary: The case of birth is different, because the פסוק says כנדתה. A נדה counts in weeks, so the word must mean two weeks, not seventy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, since it is written 'as in her menstruation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that in this פסוק the context decides how to read the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדה is טמאה for seven days, one week. Comparing the birth to נדה shows the פסוק is counting in weeks, so שבעים must mean 'two weeks.' The spelling as 'seventy' has no role here at all.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different there
as in her menstruation, like her time as a נדה

steps.whatToRemember: Combining the reading and the spelling only works when the פסוק leaves room for it. Here the word כנדתה shows the פסוק means weeks.

phrases.english: It is different there,
since it is written 'as in her menstruation.'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, ויקרא 12:5. A נדה is counted in weeks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the context of the פסוק decides the reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The spelling 'seventy' should count together with 'two weeks.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of כנדתה, the פסוק counts in weeks, so it means only fourteen days.

steps.title: A tanna's source for בית הלל from the three times 'and he shall atone' appears
steps.stepSummary: A new section starts: a תנא brings support for בית הלל that one placement of blood works even for a חטאת. He uses the three times וכפר appears in the פסוקים about a חטאת, and says it is because of a logical reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a תנא brings it from here: 'And he shall atone,' 'and he shall atone,' 'and he shall atone' — because of the logical reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new source for בית הלל's view. It quotes the start of a ברייתא, and the explanation of 'because of the reasoning' continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכפר appears three times, for the חטאת of a נשיא, a goat, and a sheep. The ברייתא says these repeats are needed 'because of the reasoning,' meaning someone might reason his way to a wrong conclusion. The details of that reasoning are about to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage of the משנה period, here the speaker in a ברייתא
brings it from here, a different source
and he (the כהן) shall atone
because of the logical reasoning

phrases.english: And a tanna brings it from here:
phrases.notes: "It" means בית הלל's rule that one placement of blood brings כפרה.

phrases.english: 'And he shall atone,' 'and he shall atone,' 'and he shall atone' —
because of the logical reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of reading and spelling and gives a different source for בית הלל.
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's rule that one placement of blood brings כפרה even for a חטאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא based on the three times וכפר appears in ויקרא chapter 4.

steps.title: A logical argument from the bird sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests learning from logic. The bird חטאת, whose blood goes below, works with one placement, so the animal חטאת, whose blood goes above, should work with one placement too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we can figure this out by logic. The תורה mentions blood placed below the red line and blood placed above it. The blood placed below works with one placement. So the blood placed above should also work with one placement.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why it needed the three פסוקים. First it shows a logical argument someone might have used instead. This is the first side of a debate that is about to start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird חטאת has its blood placed below the red line, and one placement is enough for it. The animal חטאת has its blood placed above the line. This argument says the animal is like the bird, so one placement should be enough for it too. This would support בית הלל without any פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it a logical argument? (an attempt to learn a rule from reasoning instead of a פסוק)
Below the red line on the altar
Above the red line on the altar
One placement of blood on the altar
He achieved atonement; the offering worked

phrases.english: For one might have said: isn't it a logical argument?
Blood is mentioned as placed below,
phrases.notes: Below the red line on the altar. This is the blood of the bird חטאת.

phrases.english: and blood is mentioned as placed above;
phrases.notes: Above the red line. This is the blood of the animal חטאת.

phrases.english: just as with the placing of blood mentioned below,
if he placed it with one placement, he achieved atonement;
so too with the blood mentioned above,
if he placed it with one placement, he achieved atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'logical reasoning' that step 4 said made the three פסוקים necessary.
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's rule that one placement is enough for an animal חטאת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to the bird חטאת, whose blood goes below the red line and works with one placement

steps.title: An opposite logical argument from the inner sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: Logic can also point the other way. The inner חטאות fail if even one placement is missing, so maybe the outer animal חטאת fails too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go this way. The תורה mentions blood placed inside, on the inner altar, and blood placed outside. Inside, if he left out even one placement, he did nothing. So outside too, if he left out one placement, he did nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives a second comparison that leads to the opposite result. It challenges the logic of the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאות whose blood goes on the inner altar must have every placement, or nothing was done. If the outer animal חטאת is compared to them, all four placements would be required. That is the opposite of בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Or go this way (bringing an opposite argument)
Inside, on the inner altar in the היכל
Outside, on the outer altar in the courtyard
He left out, he was missing
He did nothing at all; the offering does not work

phrases.english: Or go this way:
Blood is mentioned as placed inside,
phrases.notes: These are the חטאות whose blood goes on the inner altar, inside the היכל.

phrases.english: and blood is mentioned as placed outside;
just as with the blood mentioned inside,
if he left out one of the placements,
he did nothing at all;
so too with the blood mentioned outside,

phrases.aramaic: חִיסֵּר אַחַת מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת, לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְלוּם.
phrases.english: if he left out one of the placements, he did nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing comparison that leads to the opposite conclusion from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The logical argument of step 5 that one placement is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different comparison, to the inner חטאות, would require every placement. So the logic of step 5 is not compelling.

steps.title: Weighing the two comparisons ends in a tie
steps.stepSummary: Each comparison has a good reason. Outside should be learned from outside, but a four-corner חטאת should be learned from a four-corner חטאת. So logic cannot decide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which one it is more like. You could say: learn outside from outside, not outside from inside. Or go this way: learn a four-corner חטאת from a four-corner חטאת, and the outer bird offering, which is not a four-corner חטאת, cannot prove anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to pick the better comparison. It finds a strong reason for each side, so neither argument can win.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird חטאת is a good match because it is also brought outside. The inner חטאות are a good match because, like the animal חטאת, their blood goes on four corners, and the bird's blood does not. Since the two reasons balance out, logic cannot settle the question. This sets up the need for a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see which one it is more like
We learn one law from another
The four corners of the altar
And let it not serve as a proof

steps.confusionAlert: Here the 'outside' that cannot prove anything is the bird חטאת, not the animal חטאת. Both are brought outside, but only the animal has blood on four corners.

phrases.english: Let us see which one it is more like.
We learn something outside from something outside,
and we do not learn something outside from something inside;
or go this way:
we learn a sin offering with four corners
phrases.notes: The animal חטאת has blood on all four corners of the altar.

phrases.english: from a sin offering with four corners;
phrases.notes: The inner חטאות also put blood on four corners, on the inner altar.

phrases.english: and let the outside one not serve as a proof,
phrases.notes: This is the bird חטאת from step 5.

phrases.english: since it is not a sin offering with four corners?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the arguments of steps 5 and 6 and shows that neither one wins.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole attempt to settle the question by logic
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each comparison has an equally strong point of likeness: same location (outside) versus same type (four-corner חטאת).

steps.title: Three times 'and he shall atone' teach that one placement is enough
steps.stepSummary: Since logic is stuck, the פסוק decides. The three times וְכִפֶּר teach that atonement works with three placements, with two, and even with only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק teaches: 'and he shall atone,' 'and he shall atone,' 'and he shall atone.' 'And he shall atone' even if he placed only three. 'And he shall atone' even if he placed only two. 'And he shall atone' even if he placed only one.
steps.whatsHappening: Because logic could not decide, the ברייתא brings the three פסוקים. They prove that one placement is enough, which is the view of בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each וְכִפֶּר lowers the number of placements needed by one: first three, then two, then one. This shows that a פסוק was truly needed here, since logic pointed both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
And he shall make atonement

keyTerms.term: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן אֶלָּא
keyTerms.meaning: Even though he placed only

steps.whatToRemember: Logic could compare the animal חטאת to the bird חטאת (one placement is enough) or to the inner חטאות (every placement is required). Since the two comparisons balance out, בית הלל's rule comes from the three times וְכִפֶּר: three, two, and even one placement still bring atonement.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern. When two logical comparisons are equally strong, the תורה's extra words are what settle the law.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And he shall make atonement," "and he shall make atonement," "and he shall make atonement"
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:כו, ד:לא, ד:לה

phrases.english: (because of the logical argument);
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets. Either way, the point is that the פסוקים were needed because logic could not decide.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְכִפֶּר״ – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן אֶלָּא שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: "and he shall make atonement": even if he placed only three,

phrases.aramaic: ״וְכִפֶּר״ – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן אֶלָּא שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: "and he shall make atonement": even if he placed only two,

phrases.aramaic: ״וְכִפֶּר״ – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן אֶלָּא אַחַת.
phrases.english: "and he shall make atonement": even if he placed only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the tie from step 7 by turning to the פסוקים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One placement of blood is enough for an animal חטאת after the fact, as בית הלל hold. This is learned from the three times וְכִפֶּר, not from logic.

steps.title: Each 'and he shall atone' is needed for its own case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from the three times וְכִפֶּר. Each one is needed to teach that its own חטאת brings atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this verse is needed for its own subject!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from step 8. It says the three וְכִפֶּר words are not extra, because each one belongs to its own חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three פסוקים are about three different חטאות. Each פסוק naturally needs to say that its own קרבן brings atonement. If every וְכִפֶּר has a job, none is left over to teach that fewer placements still work.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for its own basic teaching, so nothing extra can be learned from it

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the חטאת fails to atone. It is only asking whether the word וְכִפֶּר is extra enough to teach something new.

phrases.english: But this is needed for itself!
phrases.notes: He means each וְכִפֶּר is needed just to say that its own חטאת brings atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source reading used in the conclusion of step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation from the three times וְכִפֶּר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word that is needed for its own plain meaning is not extra, so it cannot be used for a further teaching

steps.title: Atonement and forgiveness are the same, so וְכִפֶּר is extra
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes בר אדא מרי. Each פסוק already says וְנִסְלַח, and forgiveness is the same as atonement. So וְכִפֶּר is extra and free to teach the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: בר אדא מרי explained it to me. The פסוק says 'and he shall atone… and he shall be forgiven.' This is atonement, and this is forgiveness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. He shows that the word וְכִפֶּר really is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק says both וְכִפֶּר and וְנִסְלַח. Since atonement and forgiveness are one thing, וְנִסְלַח alone would have been enough for the plain teaching. That leaves the three וְכִפֶּר words free to teach that the חטאת works even with fewer placements.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement
Forgiveness
And he shall be forgiven

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: בַּר אַדָּא מָרִי אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי –
phrases.english: Rava said: Bar Adda Mari explained it to me:
The verse says: "And he shall atone… and he shall be forgiven"

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא כַּפָּרָה זוֹ הִיא סְלִיחָה.
phrases.english: This is atonement, this is forgiveness.
phrases.notes: He means they are the same thing, so the תורה did not need both words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בַּר אַדָּא מָרִי אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the word is extra because another word in the same פסוק already covers its plain meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each וְכִפֶּר is needed to teach that its own חטאת atones
steps.terutzMaskana: וְנִסְלַח already teaches that, so the three times וְכִפֶּר are extra and teach about the placements

steps.title: Maybe the extra words allow blood placed low on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a different meaning for the three extra וְכִפֶּר. Maybe they teach that all four placements still work even when some or all are put on the lower part of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'and he shall atone' even if he put only three above and one below; 'and he shall atone' even if he put only two below and two above; 'and he shall atone' even if he did not put any above, only below!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to read the three extra words. If this reading is right, the proof for one placement falls away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words do not have to be about missing placements. They might be about wrong placements, meaning the כהן did all four but put some on the lower half of the מזבח. Each וְכִפֶּר would allow one more placement to move below, until all four are below.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, read it this way
Above, on the upper part of the מזבח where a חטאת's blood belongs
Below, on the lower part of the מזבח

phrases.english: Say: "And he shall atone"

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן אֶלָּא

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra words could just as well teach that wrongly placed blood still works, so they do not prove that missing placements are allowed

steps.title: That would cancel the four corners
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר יצחק rejects the suggestion. If all the blood could go below, the Torah's rule of four corners would mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר יצחק said: If so, you have canceled the law of the four corners.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר יצחק tries to answer the challenge of step 11. He says the suggested reading cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The corners (קרנות) are on the top part of the מזבח. If the blood could all be put below, the corners would never be used. The תורה's command about the four corners would be emptied out.

keyTerms.meaning: You have canceled
The four corners on top of the מזבח, where a חטאת's blood is placed

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, בִּיטַּלְתָּ תּוֹרַת אַרְבַּע קְרָנוֹת.
phrases.english: If so, you have canceled the law of the four corners.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר יִצְחָק: אִם כֵּן, בִּיטַּלְתָּ תּוֹרַת אַרְבַּע קְרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the alternate reading because it would empty out a Torah rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra וְכִפֶּר words allow blood to be placed below
steps.terutzMaskana: That cannot be, because then the four corners would never be needed

steps.title: If the Torah says so, let the corners be canceled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רב אדא בר יצחק. If the פסוק itself teaches that below works, there is nothing wrong with the corner rule losing its force.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the Merciful One says so, let them be canceled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אדא בר יצחק's answer, so the question from step 11 still needs an answer. Step 14 gives it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule can have exceptions if the תורה itself makes them. If the extra words really say that blood below still works, then the תורה chose to weaken the corner rule. So 'it cancels the corners' is not a real reason to refuse the reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Let them be canceled

phrases.english: But if the Merciful One says so, let them be canceled!
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the four corners. If the תורה itself said it, there is no problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects רב אדא בר יצחק's reason
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah itself can create an exception to its own rule, so 'it cancels the corners' does not disprove the reading

steps.title: Three extra words point to the corners
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the real answer. Three extra words must be about something that comes in threes, and that is the corners: up to three of the four may be skipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the thing that needs three? You must say: these are the corners.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the question from step 11. He shows that the three extra וְכִפֶּר words fit the corners, so they teach that placements may be left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number of extra words must match the number of cases they teach. Skipping corners fits exactly: three missing, then two, then one, while one corner is always still placed. The 'below' reading of step 11 would need four steps to reach 'all below' (three and one, two and two, one and three, none and four), but there are only three words.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the thing
You must say, it can only be

steps.whatToRemember: The three extra וְכִפֶּר words teach that a חטאת works even if one, two, or three of the four corners were skipped. That is the source for בית הלל that one placement is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main defense of the source for בית הלל's rule that one placement is enough. The גמרא tests it again in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שָׁלֹשׁ?
phrases.english: Rava said: What is the thing that needs three?
phrases.notes: He means the three extra times וְכִפֶּר must match something that comes in threes.

phrases.english: You must say: these are the corners.
phrases.notes: Three of the four corners can be skipped, and one corner is still placed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 rejected רב אדא בר יצחק's answer, gives a new answer to step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three extra times וְכִפֶּר refer to the corners and teach that atonement works even if only one of the four corners received blood

steps.title: Maybe the extra words allow mixing above and below
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the three extra וְכִפֶּר words could teach that a mix of placements above and below the red line still works. All four corners would still be used, so the corner rule would not be lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'and he shall make atonement' even if he placed only one above and three below!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer by giving another way to read the three extra words וְכִפֶּר. Each word would allow a different split of the four placements between the upper and lower parts of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא rejected the 'below' reading because reaching 'all below' would need four words. This new reading stops before 'all below,' so it needs only three: 3 and 1, 2 and 2, and 1 and 3. That fits the three words exactly, and some blood still goes above every time.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead / maybe we should read it this way
Above, on the upper half of the מזבח (above the red line)
Below, on the lower half of the מזבח
He placed (the blood)

phrases.english: Say: “and he shall make atonement”
phrases.notes: This is the last of three readings, one for each extra וְכִפֶּר: three above and one below, two and two, and one and three.

phrases.english: even though he did not place
except one above
and three below!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: ״וְכִפֶּר״ – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן אֶלָּא אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְשָׁלֹשׁ לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 14 with a different use for the three extra words, one that fits his count of three.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the three extra וְכִפֶּר words teach that up to three corners may be skipped.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three extra words could just as well match three ways of splitting the placements between above and below (3-1, 2-2, 1-3). That gives exactly three cases, so רבא's count does not force the corners reading.

steps.title: Blood is never split half above and half below
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we never find a blood service where part of the blood goes above and part goes below. So the mixing reading cannot be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not find blood where half of it goes above and half of it goes below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the mixing reading. It points out that a split between above and below does not exist anywhere in the תורה's blood services.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every blood service goes either all above or all below. A reading that creates a brand-new split pattern has nothing like it anywhere else. So the extra words must teach something else, which brings us back to רבא's corners.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not find (no case like this exists)
Blood (of sacrifices)
Half of them

phrases.english: We do not find blood
of which half is above
and half is below.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא מָצִינוּ דָּמִים שֶׁחֶצְיָין לְמַעְלָה וְחֶצְיָין לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: No precedent: the suggested pattern never exists in any blood service.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three extra words could allow a mix of placements above and below.
steps.terutzMaskana: A split of blood between above and below never happens, so the words cannot mean that.

steps.title: But on יום כיפור there was one up and seven down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim from a משנה about יום כיפור. There the כהן גדול sprinkled once upward and seven times downward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there really no such case? But we learned in a משנה: he sprinkled from it once upward and seven times downward!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 16. It brings a case from the יום כיפור service where blood does seem to be split between up and down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the קדש הקדשים, the כהן גדול sprinkled the blood one time upward and seven times downward. That looks like exactly the split that step 16 said never happens.

keyTerms.meaning: He sprinkled
From it (from the blood)

phrases.english: And is there not?! But didn't we learn:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in יומא about the כהן גדול sprinkling inside the קדש הקדשים on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: he sprinkled from it once upward
and seven times downward!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וְהָתְנַן: הִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְשֶׁבַע לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the general rule stated in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that blood is never split between above and below.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה describes sprinkling one upward and seven downward, which looks like a split between above and below.

steps.title: It was like someone whipping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the יום כיפור sprinklings were not split between two areas. They were done 'like a מַצְלִיף'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like one who whips.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in one word: the sprinkling was done כְּמַצְלִיף. It will explain the word in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'up' and 'down' in that משנה do not mean two separate areas, one above and one below. They describe the direction of the hand while sprinkling in one place. So it is not a case of half above and half below, and the rule from step 16 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who whips (strikes with a lash)

phrases.english: Like one who whips.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the up and down sprinklings were not in two separate areas.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One upward and seven downward means blood split between above and below.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sprinklings were aimed like whip strokes, one below the other, not split into upper and lower areas.

steps.title: What does 'like a whipper' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word כְּמַצְלִיף means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'like one who whips' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the word in the last answer means. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 18 depends on this unusual word. Before the answer can be accepted, the learner needs to know what motion it describes.

keyTerms.meaning: What (is the meaning of)?

phrases.english: What is “like one who whips”?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word used in the answer of step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of motion the word כְּמַצְלִיף describes.

steps.title: רב יהודה shows the whipping motion
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה shows with his hand what the word means: like a person giving lashes, one stroke under the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה demonstrated: like one who gives lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by acting it out with his hand. He shows the motion of someone giving lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person giving lashes does not hit the same spot again and again. Each stroke lands just under the one before it. In the same way, the sprinklings formed one line going downward in one area. They were not two separate groups, one on top and one on the bottom.

keyTerms.meaning: Showed / demonstrated (with a hand motion)
Like one who gives lashes

steps.whatToRemember: The יום כיפור sprinklings of one up and seven down were done like whip strokes, one under the other. They do not show blood split between above and below.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda demonstrated:
like one who gives lashes.
phrases.notes: He showed it with his hand: each stroke lands a little below the last one, not on the same spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כְּמַצְלִיף means the motion of someone giving lashes, with each stroke aimed just below the last.

steps.title: Another challenge: seven sprinklings on 'טׇהֳרוֹ' of the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second challenge from the יום כיפור service. The כהן גדול sprinkled seven times on 'טׇהֳרוֹ' of the inner מזבח, after placing blood on its corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sprinkled on the 'טׇהֳרוֹ' of the מזבח seven times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case that might show blood split between two places. This step sets up the next challenge, and the answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור, the blood was put on the corners of the inner golden מזבח, and then sprinkled seven times on 'טׇהֳרוֹ' of the מזבח. If the corners count as one place and 'טׇהֳרוֹ' as another, this could look like the split that step 16 said never happens. To judge the challenge, we will need to know what 'טׇהֳרוֹ' means.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'its clearness'; a place on the מזבח, explained next
The altar (here, the inner golden altar)
Times

phrases.english: he sprinkled on the “tohoro” of the altar
phrases.notes: Read this with the same question from step 17, 'And is there not? But didn't we learn.' This is another משנה in יומא.

phrases.english: seven times.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִזָּה עַל טׇהֳרוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17's challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a second challenge against the rule of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 16 that blood is never split between two levels.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On יום כיפור, blood went both on the corners of the inner מזבח and seven times on its 'טׇהֳרוֹ', which may be a split between two areas.
